summary: Batched job deduplication logic caused missing postback credits for multi-org batch
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that a scheduled batched embedding job completed on 2026-03-11 but did not receive the expected meter credit adjustments. The job runs across multiple subaccounts; customer expects per-subaccount credit back for cache hits and duplicate suppression. Instead, only a partial credit arrived and a subset of subaccounts show no postback recorded.

Impact:
- LexiAssist reports $120 of missing credits on the March 11 provisional invoice.
- Affects one recurring multi-org batch (nightly ingest) and causes under-crediting for three subaccounts leading to downstream billing alerts.

Environment:
prod clusters in us-east-1, dedicated pool 'lexi-dedicated-2', batch scheduler v1.14.2, postback-processor v2.3.1.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Submit multi-org batched embedding job with 4 subaccounts attached (GUIDs provided in logs).
2) Allow job to finish; verify batch completion event emitted to postback queue.
3) Confirm postback-processor consumes completion event and posts meter adjustments; expected 4 postbacks (one per subaccount).
4) Observe only 1 postback persisted; other 3 were dropped by deduplication step.

Observed logs / snippets:
- batch-run-id: br-20260311-98ad
- postback-queue messages show single canonical postback with dedup_key "br-20260311-98ad-canonical".
- postback-processor log excerpt: "INFO dedupe: normalized_key=%s canonical_owner=org-1214 from=org-1102 dropped=true reason=owner-normalization"

Additional context:
Customer uses per-subaccount attribution for internal cost centers. This batch was migrated last month to the new microbatch pipeline; they first noticed discrepancy after migration.
comments: 2026-03-12 08:17 - Customer (Ben Harlow, LexiAssist): We ran our nightly ingest and saw only one credit applied to the parent account. This used to credit each subaccount separately. Can you confirm why credits were consolidated?

2026-03-12 13:45 - SRE (Miguel Santos): Initial analysis: postback-processor dedupe normalization collapsed owner metadata when parent org present. Suspect normalization bug introduced in v2.3.1. Reproduced locally with a test harness: dedupe normalized all subaccounts to parent-org id when parent metadata present.

2026-03-12 15:20 - Engineering (Chen Wei): Created PR to stop owner normalization during dedupe for batched jobs: github.com/redwood-inference/postback-service/pull/4321. Deployed PR to staging; tests show per-subaccount postbacks preserved.

2026-03-13 09:05 - Support (Aisha Kaur): Updated customer: provisional credit of $120 applied to parent invoice while we complete root cause; backfill scheduled for 2026-03-15. Will keep you posted on timeline.
2026-03-13 11:12 - Customer (Ben Harlow): Thanks — please ensure the backfill applies credits to the original subaccount line items rather than parent-level. Need this for internal chargebacks.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-12 - Reproducer: run multi-org batch through postback-processor v2.3.1 with parent_org metadata set -> dedupe normalization step sets canonical_owner to parent org and marks other owner postbacks as duplicates.

2026-03-12 - Hypothesis: owner-normalization was added to reduce duplicate cost for mirrored jobs but didn't account for per-subaccount attribution; edge-case triggered during migration to microbatch pipeline.

2026-03-12 - Partial finding: Message payload from batch scheduler included both owner and parent_owner fields; normalization code preferred parent_owner when present. For multi-org batches parent_owner exists and collapsed keys.
2026-03-12 - Staging test: Deploy PR/4321 which bypasses normalization for messages with field 'multi_org=true' — per-subaccount postbacks preserved in staging and credits generated correctly.
2026-03-12 - Customer impact estimate: 1 nightly run affected over last 7 days => ~$840 total missing credits across accounts; LexiAssist's accounting flagged $120 on the parent invoice.
2026-03-13 - Next steps: schedule backfill reprocessing of deduped messages in prod; ensure credit memos are created per subaccount; deploy fix to prod after smoke tests.
resolution: Pending - Mitigation steps taken: provisional credit of $120 issued to customer's parent invoice on 2026-03-13 to prevent immediate billing disruption. Engineering created and merged PR 4321 to fix owner-normalization; change deployed to staging and passed smoke tests. Planned rollout: 2026-03-15 02:00 UTC to prod with short maintenance window. Post-deploy actions: run backfill job to reprocess dropped postbacks for batch-run-id br-20260311-98ad and previous 7 days, create per-subaccount credit memos, and notify customer when completed. Assigned to Miguel Santos for prod deploy and backfill coordination. Final resolution ETA: 2026-03-16.
